countsMean.frames: The sweep's own frame count, asserted by `check-evidence.mjs` against the frames on disk that fall outside any declared `supplementary` set - 640 at this commit, and the assertion is the definition rather than a restatement of it: 749 `.webp` are committed and the sixteen `supplementary` sets below account for 109 of them, leaving 640. This PR is where two of those terms moved, and both moved for the same reason - a declared set is a claim the tree can no longer regenerate. The retired popover's twenty frames (`chat-run-details`) lost their stories with the surface itself, and the live reader pair (`chat-run-panel-live`) needs a real backend and a running child. Before them the arithmetic was 594 swept + 54 run-panel frames added by this branch; the six stories added in the review round are the further twelve. `check-evidence.mjs` is what confirms every term; the figures are recorded here because a reader who cannot re-derive them has no way to tell a reconciled manifest from one that was edited until the gate passed.
countsMean.surfaces: `capture-evidence.mjs`'s `STORIES.length` at the head above - 118 entries, of which 33 are this PR's run-panel surfaces (27 as first drafted, six added in the review round: the two reader absences, the brief, the unaddressed row and the two halves of the MCP dot's discipline).
countsMean.themes: `THEMES.length` - the twelve brand palettes; the live pair is the two brand themes only, because it proves behaviour rather than colour.

supplementary.source: the REAL built Electron app: npx electron . from each tree's own out/ (built with pnpm build, so import.meta.env.DEV is false and the development-only Chat|Raw tab strip does not exist), against an isolated local-operator serve on its own port, seeded from out/evidence-harness/seed.mjs and paired through a shared LOCAL_OPERATOR_DESKTOP_TOKEN; driven over raw CDP by out/evidence-harness/app-drive.mjs. The before tree is a detached worktree at a09f2e6f4 with the same script and the same backend.
supplementary.why: The claim is a CLICK that both opens a conversation and writes its title into the catalogue store the sidebar reads, and the two surfaces it moves between - the sidebar row and the chat header - have no story (the sidebar's absence from the sweep is recorded in docs/evidence/sidebar-new-chat), so no sweep can re-derive these frames and Storybook would have to fake both the store write and the press. Captured from the built app rather than electron-vite dev because in dev the development-only Chat|Raw tab strip paints over the header: the first attempt at this evidence produced byte-identical before/after frames with a correct DOM and the subject covered.

The claims are a real pointer hover and a click that stages a draft. Storybook can force the revealed class but not produce the hover, and a staged draft is store state a fixture would have to fake, so these are captured from the running app against an isolated seeded backend instead. The sidebar has no story, so re-running the sweep cannot re-derive them; docs/evidence/sidebar-new-chat/README.md carries the re-capture procedure.

supplementary.source: headless Chrome over CDP, driven by `node scripts/diff-body-evidence.mjs`: the shipped `applyHistoryPage` reducer and the shipped `CanonicalTranscript` over a real durable history page read from one real session's `transcript.jsonl` in the local store (`--session` and `--anchor` are required arguments; the id is deliberately not committed)
supplementary.why: The story renders a TranscriptRecord this repository built, so it proves the component. This set starts one layer earlier, at the bytes `/v1/desktop/sessions/{id}/history` serves — the stored rows, serialised verbatim by `read_transcript_page` — and runs them through the shipped reducer, which is what proves the payload reaches pixels: the durable row's own encoding, the extraction of `provider_payload.details.diff`, the identity gate and the args-drop rule. It cannot be re-derived by the sweep, and the payload itself is deliberately NOT committed: the harness writes it to a temp file and deletes it. Re-run with `node scripts/diff-body-evidence.mjs --session=<id> --anchor=<row id>` (see docs/evidence/write-edit-diff/README.md).

The only frames in this tree rendered against a REAL /v1/desktop/usage response rather than story fixtures: 11 provider reports and 28 windows as the local backend actually returned them, which is what proves the ported view renders the wire shape and not merely its own fixtures. Storybook cannot produce them (the payload needs the desktop bearer), so the sweep cannot re-derive these two frames. Account identities are redacted shape-preservingly by the capture script; every number, window, tier, unit and staleness value is the backend's own. docs/evidence/chat-usage/README.md carries the re-capture procedure. RE-CAPTURED for review round 1 from the same real response (replayed via `--payload`, since this machine's backend now returns zero reports and cannot re-derive it): the committed pair was the evidence for the staleness-baseline and description defects, so leaving it would have shipped a picture of the bug beside its fix. ROUND 3: a genuine live refill was attempted (live=true&refresh=true with the server's own bearer, plus explicit per-provider asks) and the backend returned zero reports for every provider - its credential view currently has no usage-reportable providers - so these two frames remain one commit stale with respect to the round-2 fold treatment. The fold at this density is evidenced by the re-derivable `chat-usage--dense` story instead.

supplementary.source: live renderer over CDP against an isolated backend
supplementary.why: Live frames from the packaged Electron app over real IPC, which Storybook cannot produce: a cold snapshot, a reload, the backend-down error path, and round 3's aggregator route plus cold-owner effort states. One theme only (localOperatorDark) because these prove BEHAVIOUR, not colour; the theme matrix is the Storybook set's job.

supplementary.source: live renderer over CDP, driven with real wheel events against a seeded backend
supplementary.why: The claims are about MOTION -- that a fling issues one page rather than one per event, and that the row under the reader holds its offset while a page lands. Neither is a property of a rendered tree, so Storybook cannot express them: they need real wheel events reaching the real scroller with a real backend answering sessions.history, and the artefact that carries the claim is the per-frame measurement JSON beside the frames rather than the frames themselves. Captured one theme deep because nothing under test is palette-dependent; the slot's own appearance is swept across all twelve by chat-older-history-slot. The before set was captured on origin/main (2217ea59a) by the QA pass and shows the click-only behaviour this change replaces. Regenerate with scripts/scroll-paging-evidence.mjs; docs/evidence/transcript-scroll-paging/README.md carries the exact seeding recipe and ports.

supplementary.source: Storybook, from the app BEFORE this change - the popover's own set, swept while its stories existed
supplementary.why: The retired popover's evidence, kept as the record of the surface this PR replaces. Its story ids are GONE from capture-evidence.mjs's STORIES, so no sweep can regenerate these frames: left undeclared they would sit inside the swept count and inside the 'every frame is a picture of the app' check while describing a surface the tree no longer has. Declared, they are what they are - a preserved record with its own provenance - and the sweep's count is honest about the set it can still take.

supplementary.source: the BUILT app (pnpm build + electron . in headless window mode) paired to an isolated backend built from the parallel backend worktree, driven over raw CDP
supplementary.why: The reader against a REAL running child, which is the one claim no story can carry: docs/run-sidebar.md 11.3 requires the live pairing for `reader-live`, because the subject is a FLOW (click a child's row, watch its durable transcript arrive over subagents.transcript, and arrive again when the child's pulse moves) and a fixture proves only the row pipeline. The backend's access log recorded 4 transcript reads for this child session while the reader was open. The procedure, the ids and the readings are in docs/evidence/chat-run-panel-live/README.md. Not sweepable by construction: it needs a model turn and a child that is running when the shutter opens.

partialCapture.note: This set is not a full sweep and does not claim to be. The run-panel surfaces were refreshed in the two brand themes by `pnpm capture-evidence.mjs --only=run-panel --themes=localOperatorDark,localOperatorLight`, and the live pair was taken by a separate harness (`docs/evidence/chat-run-panel-live/README.md`). Nothing else was re-taken: the other 600-odd frames describe surfaces this change does not touch. The frames were taken from this working tree minutes before its final lint tidy (a regex literal hoisted to a module constant, with no rendered effect); `srcTree` names the committed tree, and `dirtyWorkingTree: true` is the record that the capture ran against the working tree rather than a commit.
partialCapture.branchAddition: Recorded here because an earlier narrowed run overwrote it (review round 1, R1-10): THIS PR added 27 run-panel surfaces and 54 frames on top of main's 574 swept frames, which is what moved the swept total 594 -> 648 before this round added a further six surfaces and twelve frames.
partialCapture.review: One batched remediation pass against the code and design round-1 findings: R1-1a's live pair (this set), R1-1b's four missing stories and R1-5's child-attachment question answered by narrowing Section 5.1, in docs/run-sidebar.md. The frames for the surfaces the fixes moved were re-taken in the same run.

reconciledNote: `frames` is the SWEEP's term and it is checked against the tree rather than asserted: `pnpm check-evidence` recomputes it from the `.webp` files on disk that fall outside every declared set, so this number cannot be right about a set that is wrong. A narrowed run writes `partialCapture` and leaves the totals alone except when it ADDS a surface; the two additions below are declared sets, not swept frames.
